title: Trigonometry: Law of Sines for SSA Practice
description: Practice setting up SSA Law of Sines problems and checking possible angle values.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 40°, a = 8, and b = 10. Which equation correctly begins solving for ∠B?
questions.explanation: Side a = 8 is opposite ∠A = 40°, and side b = 10 is opposite ∠B, so sin B / 10 = sin 40° / 8.

questions.question: In an SSA Law of Sines problem, why should you check 180° minus the calculator angle?
options: The supplement may have the same sine and may form a second triangle.
The supplement always gives the correct triangle.
The calculator angle is never valid in SSA.
Triangle angles must always include one obtuse angle.
questions.explanation: Sine has the same value for an acute angle and its obtuse supplement, so an SSA case may have two possible angles.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 40°, a = 8, and b = 10. The calculator gives ∠B ≈ 53.5°. What supplementary angle should also be checked?
In △ABC, ∠A = 40°, a = 8, and b = 10. Which statement is true?
options: The information is SAS, not SSA.
questions.explanation: sin B ≈ 0.8035 gives B ≈ 53.5° or 126.5°. Both leave a positive third angle with A = 40°, so two triangles are possible.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 42°, a = 11, and b = 8. The calculator gives ∠B ≈ 29.1°. Why is 150.9° not valid?
options: It is not a supplement of 29.1°.
The side b must always be the longest side.
Obtuse angles are never allowed in SSA.
questions.explanation: The angle sum 42° + 150.9° = 192.9°, which leaves no positive third angle.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 35°, a = 4, and b = 9. What does sin B ≈ 1.29 mean?
questions.explanation: A real angle cannot have a sine greater than 1, so the given measurements cannot form a triangle.

questions.question: In an SSA case, if both B and 180° - B leave a positive third angle, two triangles are possible.
questions.explanation: Both angle choices can fit the same sine value, so both produce valid triangles if the angle sums stay below 180°.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 30°, a = 6, and b = 10. Find the smaller possible value of ∠B to the nearest tenth of a degree.
questions.explanation: sin B = 10 sin 30° / 6 = 0.8333..., so the smaller possible angle is B ≈ 56.4°.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 30°, a = 6, and b = 10. Find the larger possible value of ∠B to the nearest tenth of a degree.
questions.explanation: The larger possible angle is the supplement of 56.4°, so B ≈ 180° - 56.4° = 123.6°.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain how you decide whether the supplementary angle is valid in an SSA problem.
questions.correctAnswer: Add the supplementary angle to the given angle. If the sum is less than 180°, it leaves a positive third angle and is valid; if the sum is 180° or more, it is not valid.
questions.explanation: A valid triangle must have three positive angles that total 180°, so the known angle plus the possible second angle must be less than 180°.
